The territory map

Click a large territory to open its upgrade box. Troop pictures are whole regiments with health bars. Click a troop for details and its Hold or Capture order. Drag to plan movement; arrows show the route until the teacher advances. In control view, unclaimed land is pale. ◆ marks a mineral deposit; Settlement pictures show levels 1–5 (red, orange, yellow, green, blue); Silver palisades or gold stone walls overlay fortified settlements. Small building icons above a settlement show the facilities built there; tap one to inspect its territory. Training troops are labeled.

Highlighted land is within range. Press Escape to cancel. Click a troop for its own Hold and Capture buttons, or use its controls above.

Drag empty map space with one finger or a mouse to pan. Pinch with two fingers to zoom. Drag your troop to plan its move; a second finger switches to map navigation. Keyboard: focus the map, then use arrows and + / −. Fit map resets the view.

Battle Lab rules

Four countries are selected to maximize the minimum straight-line distance between their starting capitals. Other countries’ land becomes unclaimed. Army setup is free and immediate, with up to six regiments per country; normal recruitment still costs resources and trains for one round.

Each country starts with one round of its owned land production. Biomes, deposits and settlement production remain; research and happiness bonuses are removed. All new income goes straight to Military before military meals. Civilian feeding, research, trade and objectives are disabled. Military food shortages still affect combat. Setup lets you choose equipment and movement without research.

Combat, movement, alliances, simultaneous damage, retreats, pursuit, captures and siege defenses use the current game rules. Spears beat cavalry, cavalry beat archers, archers beat spears. Artillery is neutral in field battles and deals double siege damage. Save a test setup to replay it. Battle Lab saves are separate from the full game.

Geography and biome import adapted from Azgaar (MIT). Geometry uses D3 Delaunay. Rule balance is ready for classroom playtesting, not a historical prediction.
